recommendation: Keep the FHIR-46924 audit commit as-is. Revisit only if OO later reverses FHIR-55651 or completes a final broader binding-strength decision that changes NutritionOrder route bindings again.
issue_request: FHIR-46924 was an Applied/Persuasive OO R6 request to add NutritionOrder.additive.routeOfAdministration as a CodeableConcept with cardinality 0..* and an Enteral Route Codes binding, originally described as extensible.
initial_application: The source history shows de8f14ac79f7ecf959a2c097ae8823ad8b8ab7a7 applied the request by adding NutritionOrder.additive.routeOfAdministration with CodeableConcept 0..*, bindingName AdditiveRouteOfAdministration, valueSet http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/enteral-route, and extensible strength. source/fhir.ini marks NutritionOrder active and records NutritionOrder.additive.routeOfAdministration as an R6 addition.
additional_context: FHIR-55651 is a later Applied/Persuasive OO decision for the same NutritionOrder route bindings. It changed NutritionOrder.additive.routeOfAdministration and NutritionOrder.enteralFormula.routeOfAdministration from extensible to preferred because the code system may not be used by all jurisdiction or implementation communities. The broader FHIR-54613 binding review remains Triaged/unresolved and was treated as background only.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source already contains the requested additive route element and value set binding; changing the binding back to extensible would undo the later FHIR-55651 decision.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied OO decision intentionally changed the additive route binding from extensible to preferred.
Broad binding-strength governance tracker related to FHIR-55651, but Triaged/unresolved and not an independent final source decision here.
